closed.evidence: All 15 changed methods verified against the jars. applyBiomeDecoration: identical logic (26.3's FeaturePlacer wrapper and startsForStructure(x,z) vs 26.2's direct feature.placeWithBiomeCheck and startsForStructure(SectionPos) are arg-shape only; seeds, step loop and index sort unchanged). createStructures/createReferences: SectionPos-vs-climateSampler threading only. clampToHeightAccessor and hasStructureChunkInRange: identical bodies. JigsawPlacement.generateJigsaw: GenerationContext construction only. The 26.3-only couldStructureExistInColumn gates (start.rs x4, jigsaw.rs addPieces heightmap branch) are outcome-neutral early-outs: the Rust implements 26.2's isValidBiome (biome at the stub position) universally at the end of structure/start.rs generate() plus per-kind checks, and a column with no valid biome anywhere necessarily fails the position check; the gates consume no RNG and the per-attempt random is discarded on rejection. getOrigin/dimension origin feeds the 26.3-only minecraft:dimension_origin placement type (DimensionOriginStructurePlacement exists in the 26.3 jars, absent from the 26.2 jars); inert under 26.2 data. spawnOriginalMobs (biome-vs-pos arg) and getMobsAt (environment attributes vs biome mob settings) have no counterpart in generator.rs; that logic lives in natural spawning / spawn_selection (item 106's scope).

ClientboundUpdateAdvancementsPacket: 26.2 sends plain AdvancementHolders (AdvancementHolder.LIST_STREAM_CODEC), 26.3 sends PositionedAdvancement with x/y floats per entry; 26.2 AdvancementNode has no x/y at all. Ported: dropped x/y from the protocol Advancement struct and codec (read+write), from the server's write_advancement (lan/advancements.rs, layout field removed), and from remote_advancements; the screen now always uses tree.layout() (26.2 repositionNodes) and visibility keys on remote.is_some() instead of positions. grant verified 26.2-form already (loot as keys resolved via registries, plain drop with no pickup delay); decorateName/toast diffs are getter renames only; trigger's ContextAwarePredicate vs LootItemCondition-Holder difference is below the Rust's predicate abstraction; no root-background validation exists in the Rust. The layout function's own 26.2 fidelity is item 10's scope (AdvancementTree.repositionNodes).

Two real ports. (1) allowOpFeatures is 26.3-only (datafix 5002 adds the flag; the 26.2 jars have no such field): 26.2's executeClickCommandsIfPresent runs RunCommand/ShowDialog/Custom unconditionally, with no CLICK_ACTIONS_DISABLED message. Removed the gate and sign_click_actions_disabled from sign_edit.rs, the allow_op_features field from SignData (block_entity.rs) and its signs.rs encode/decode, and the canonical-NBT passthrough (block_entity_nbt.rs). The datafix-5002 upgrade code in fixes_c.rs stays (version-conversion machinery). (2) Wax-on sound: 26.2's HoneycombItem (useOn and tryApplyToSign) fires only level event 3003; the sound comes from the client's LevelEventHandler 3003 (playLocalSound). 26.3 moved it to explicit playSound calls. Moved the sound into block_particle_event (play_unshared, so the serving game does not capture it as a sound packet too) and removed the six explicit plays (sign applicator, dispenser, game.rs use_tool incl. the wax_on_sound helper, copper golem, remote prediction x2); the double chest's second sound now comes from the other half's event, as in 26.2. Verified no-change: canExecuteClickCommands (waxed + click events), updateSignText/setMessages/updateText/setText (identical logic), TextFieldHelper.keyPressed (logic identical; SDL/GLFW codes abstracted by winit), SignApplicator.canApplyToSign, setMessage (equality check is a no-op optimisation), openTextEdit, useItemOn/useWithoutItem (slot enum vs boolean; hasEditableText same logic both versions). The SignUpdate packet codec was already in 26.2 form (four strings + front bool).

Bubble column: 26.2 applies the effect server-side only with no entity event (up: velocity.y = 2.7 with a player aboard, 0.6 without; down: -0.7 then eject passengers); 26.3 broadcasts events 71/72 and the client applies 0.6. Removed the event constants, handle_bubble_column_effect and remote_boat_event; tick_boat_bubble_column now applies directly. deltaRotation: 26.2's AbstractBoat.tick keeps it on the non-authoritative branch (26.3 zeroes it) — removed both zeroings. Rider rotation ported to 26.2's positionRider/clampRotation (yaw += delta, clamp ±105° around the boat's yaw with yRotO moving, head snaps to yaw then takes the animal offset); 26.3 snaps mob yaw to body instead. No-change: renderers (poseStack.rotateDegrees vs mulPose), ServerLevel.tickNonPassenger (commonTick vs inline setOldPosAndRot+tickCount++), getControllingPassenger (identical), onPassengerTurned (same outcome). Cargo check clean.

Three 26.3-only features removed. (1) Projectile.can_break: 26.2's mayBreak is impact tag + projectiles_can_break_blocks only, no adventure predicate; removed Arrow.can_break + save/load, the mob-arrow predicate gate in projectile_breaks_block (now mob_griefing alone), projectile_predicate_supported, and the predicate tests (denied_hits now expects the mob arrow to break the flower). (2) Entity.invulnerableTime as a saved temp-invulnerability timer: in 26.2 the field IS the hurt cooldown (never saved, never feeds isInvulnerable); removed the field, save/load, tick decrement, conversion/cure copies; is_invulnerable is now the flag alone; skeleton-trap sets the cooldown (60); hurt-cooldown test kept and renamed; parity harness docs rewritten to 26.2 semantics. (3) Skeleton FreezingTime: 26.2 saves/loads only StrayConversionTime; removed the save/load and updated the round-trip tests. ConversionType.convertCommon: 26.2 copies only the invulnerable flag (26.3 copies flag + timer). Zombie.tick: 26.2 does NOT stop a started conversion on leaving the water (26.3's ConversionTracker did) — removed the stop branch; fixed the start value 300 -> 301 (off-by-one vs both versions; vanilla starts at 300, counter2 is time+1, as the skeleton's 301). Skeleton.tick order (conversion before super.tick) vs the Rust's mid-AI-step placement is a noted sub-tick micro-divergence, not ported. Deflection verified no-change: REVERSE arithmetic equal at every call site (arrow-refused -0.1, trident -0.01/-0.1/-0.01, breeze -0.5, border -0.1), AIM_DEFLECT power 1.0 everywhere, MOMENTUM_DEFLECT has no vanilla callers in 26.2, deflect's client-side application unobservable (client arrow ticks with empty targets), hitTargetOrDeflectSelf air-block NONE unreachable (Rust clip never returns air), projectileReceivesSideEffectsOnHit is 26.3-only and the Rust's unconditional turn-back matches 26.2. Pre-existing gaps vs BOTH versions, noted not ported: arrows/fishing hooks stick on the world border instead of bouncing (shouldBounceOnWorldBorder), a drowned's saved InWaterTime (vanilla saves the loaded value in water, Rust saves -1). Cargo check clean; protocol tests 443/2 (sandbox pair).

GuiGraphicsExtractor blit/fill/itemCooldown/map/textHighlight byte-identical between 26.2 and 26.3 (flagged only for the RenderPipeline/GpuSampler/GpuTextureView import move from com.mojang.renderpearl.api to com.mojang.blaze3d). Tooltip: 26.3 adds extraSpaceAfterFirstLine (item tooltips only); 26.2 always adds the 2px after the first line, which the Rust already implements for all tooltips (tooltip_size 1 line 8.0, n lines 10.0n; tooltip_box ly += 12.0 first line else 10.0). EditBox.keyPressed: SDL-vs-GLFW keycode renumbering only, identical logic; the Rust uses winit KeyCodes. capturesInput() is 26.3-only with no Rust references; preedit/setTextInputArea has no Rust modelling. AbstractSliderButton.extractWidgetRenderState identical.

PORTED (1) use-cooldown side effects: in 26.2 applyAfterUseComponentSideEffects is called ONLY from finishUsingItem and releaseUsing (identical in both versions); 26.3 added the call to ItemStack.use and useOn. The 26.2 item data has use_cooldown only on chorus_fruit (1.0s, a timed consume, still applies via finishUsingItem), ender_pearl (1.0s) and wind_charge (0.5s) — and neither EnderpearlItem.use nor WindChargeItem.use sets a cooldown directly in 26.2, so pearls/charges have NO cooldown in 26.2. Removed the apply_use_cooldown calls from throw_item (pearl + wind-charge branches), the guest instant-use path (remote.rs), the 0-tick consumable path (using_item.rs: Consumable.startConsuming calls onConsume directly, not finishUsingItem), and the useOn placement path (use_hand.rs). Kept complete_using_item, mod_release_using and remote_complete_using (finishUsingItem/releaseUsing, correct in both). (2) Mooshroom stew particles: 26.2 loops level.addParticle per particle (x + nextDouble()/2, getY(0.5), z + nextDouble()/2, velocity (0, nextDouble()/5, 0), 4 EFFECT fresh / 2 SMOKE fed); ported from the single sendParticles broadcast to per-particle particles.add + count-0 LAN packets. Verified no-change: SpeleothemBlock/ChorusFlowerBlock.onProjectileHit (only the mayBreak signature, covered by item 97), BreakDoorGoal.tick (isSwinging/swingForAttack vs swinging field/swing, rename only), ItemStack hurtAndBreak/applyDamage/hurtWithoutBreaking (identical logic; onBreak callback type ItemStack vs Item only), addDetailsToTooltip (26.3's sign-text lines have no Rust counterpart; 26.2 has no sign-text components on items, pinned by rank 1), ThrownItemRenderer.submit (rotate vs mulPose rename only). Notes: remote.rs:9286 knowledge-book apply_use_cooldown is a no-op (no item has both RECIPES and USE_COOLDOWN), left; the RECIPES component id 68 is 26.3's numbering (item 8's scope). The LevelParticles codec still carries 26.3's per-axis max_speed + randomization fields — item 104's scope. Mooshroom y stays feet+0.5 (vanilla getY(0.5) is feet+0.7 for a 1.4-high mooshroom; pre-existing approximation in both versions) and the draws use the level random, not the mob's (same convention as death_poof).

PORTED (1) Spectator crosshair: 26.2's Hud.canRenderCrosshairForSpectator uses level.getBlockState(pos).getMenuProvider(level, pos) != null for blocks; 26.3's BlockBehaviour.showAsInteractableInSpectatorMode adds '|| state.getBlock() instanceof Portal'. Removed the portal branch (nether_portal/end_portal/end_gateway) from block_interactable_for_spectator in game/hand.rs, so a spectator looking at a portal gets no crosshair in 26.2. (2) Health blink: 26.2 reads player.invulnerableTime > 0 (the hurt cooldown, per item 97); 26.3 renamed the field damageCooldownTime. The value passed (p.health.hurt.cooldown > 0) was already the 26.2-correct one; renamed the HealthInputs field damage_cooldown to hurt_cooldown (doc, layout, game.rs caller, hud_fixture.rs probe) to match 26.2's vocabulary. Verified no-change: the other 10 Hud extract* methods are byte-identical (flagged only because the file changed) and ExperienceBar.extractBackground has an empty diff.

26.3-only level events removed: digging 2019/2020 (26.2's MultiPlayerGameMode plays the block hit sound client-side every 4th destroy tick, no crack particles while mining; startDestroyBlock plays nothing), potion 1053/1054 (26.2 sends only 2002/2007 with the splash sound at the end of the handler), 2014/2016/2017/2018 (single-block teleport trails, shulker/chorus/enderman). 2015 kept as the sim's internal channel only (never broadcast): 26.2's DragonEggBlock spawns the 128 portal particles client-side, not as an event. TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect: directional_particles removed everywhere (TeleportConsume struct, JSON reader, item_sync wire codec, hash gameplay/skip/exact, fixture, oracle) — 26.2's record is (diameter) only, randomTeleport(x,y,z,boolean) has no tag, no CONSUMABLE_DOES_NOT_TELEPORT_TO. LevelParticles codec ported to the 26.2 packet: one scalar maxSpeed, no randomization field; QueuedParticle scalar speed; spread is gaussian around the position (both ways) for count>0, velocity = maxSpeed*dist for count==0; adapter down/up updated (largest-of-three test rewritten to a single-speed test). Powder-snow snowflake now a count-0 packet (26.2 spawns it client-side); evaporation smoke local draw gaussian. Fireworks (createFireworks playSound param), tickNonPassenger, getRelativeTickSpeed: no-change. Hash test cases re-keyed with values computed by a Java probe against the 26.2 jars (validated by exact reproduction of the 26.3 can_place_on hash). Verification: cargo check --workspace --all-targets 0 warnings/errors; horizon-protocol tests 443 passed / 2 failed (sandbox-network pair only); horizon-client --lib lan_particles 5 passed; tools/test_teleport_consume_parity.py PASSED (client and server 278,190 output lines match Rust). Jar diffs /tmp/item104a.diff (ClientLevel), /tmp/item104b.diff (LevelEventHandler), /tmp/item104c.diff (BlockUtil), /tmp/item104g.diff, /tmp/item104h.diff, /tmp/item104k.diff, /tmp/item104l.diff, /tmp/item104n.diff, /tmp/item104o.diff.

StrongholdPieces: StructurePiecesBuilder renamed to StructurePieceAccessor (26.2's name) with identical logic, including PortalRoom.createPiece and the 112-block bound. StrongholdStructure.generatePieces: empty diff. FixedBiomeSource: BiomeResolver/createResolver vs NoiseBiomeSource/getNoiseBiome is an API-shape change; findBiomeHorizontal and getBiomesWithin bodies are identical (single biome, allowed-test). No behavioural difference anywhere in the item.

GrassBlock.performBonemeal: 26.2 rolls the tall-grass chance as random.nextInt(10)==0 and the flower chance as random.nextInt(8)==0; 26.3 uses nextFloat()<0.1F and nextFloat()<0.125F — same probabilities but different RNG draws, so the sequence diverges after them. Ported grass_bonemeal_effect to next_int(10)==0 / next_int(8)==0 in the same short-circuit positions. The offset walk already used next_int(3)-1 (26.2's form; 26.3's nextIntBetweenInclusive draws identically). SeaPickle/GrowingPlantHead/BoneMealItem diffs are the BonemealSource parameter (26.3-only, signature only) and setBlockAndUpdate vs setBlock(...,3) (identical); the Rust has no source parameter. The flower/grass placement structure (ConfiguredFeature, empty-list fall-through) already matches 26.2.

26.3's KeyEvent has a keycode field and shortcutKey() (SDL keycode, layout-dependent letter); 26.2's KeyEvent has a scancode field and no shortcutKey — the edit shortcuts compare input() against the GLFW codes A/C/V/X (65/67/86/88) and the narrator hotkey against GLFW_KEY_B (66), i.e. by physical position. Ported shortcut_letter to take only the physical key and map all 26 letter keys by US-layout position (on AZERTY the Q-position key is Q, not the A it types); updated the 4 call sites (game/clipboard.rs edit_shortcut, game/narrator.rs, game/startup_menu.rs x2) and rewrote the test to pin position-decides. charTyped/textInput diffs are the NarrationTrigger import only; get/setClipboard differ only in the window/error-callback plumbing (arboard behaviour unchanged); the F3 debug keys (handleChunkDebugKeys, MultiDrawIndirect/translucency toggles, wireframe check) live in debug_keys, not this module. cargo check clean, horizon-client-input tests 128/0.

CloudRenderer#prepare + #renderOit: 26.3 split 26.2's render() into prepare() (compute + build mesh) + render()/renderOit() (draw, incl. the new OIT path) and moved the render API from Blaze3D to RenderPearl. The geometry the Rust ports — radius cells (range*16/12), cloud offset (gameTime % (width*400) + partialTicks), cell math — is identical in both versions.

AbstractFurnaceBlockEntity: 26.2 has no speedMultiplier (field, save key and getSpeedMultiplier all 26.3-only); save times are shorts (getShortOr/putShort), not ints; getBurnDuration takes FuelValues only (no cooking_fuel component); consumeFuel takes no level/pos and drops nothing (remainder takes the slot only once the stack is used up, else lost); completion is cookingTimer == cookingTotalTime (26.3 uses >=); getTotalCookTime is the recipe's cookingTime directly. Ported: removed Furnace.speed, the drops param from FurnaceCooking::tick, Providers.speed; save/NBT canonicalisation use shorts; completion ==; furnace_fixture drops speed. canTakeItemThroughFace (water_bucket|bucket) and canPlaceItem (burn_time > 0) were already 26.2-form in machines.rs. Gap: VanillaFurnaceOracle still reflects speedMultiplier, so the furnace harness cannot run against 26.2 until the oracle + driver are ported.

SignText#hasAnyClickCommands: 26.3 takes (boolean shouldFilter), 26.2 takes (Player player) and reads player.isTextFilteringEnabled(); both scan getMessages(filter) for a RUN_COMMAND click event. The Rust has_any_click_commands checks the stored click events and keeps no filtered text, so the filter source is unobservable in either version.

MeshData#decodeQuadCentroids: bodies byte-identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (opposite-corner midpoint); the added/removed flag is only the VertexFormat type moving from com.mojang.renderpearl.api.vertex to com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex. The Rust references it in a comment only (translucency.rs:4).

Ingredient#display: 26.3 always returns TagSlotDisplay; 26.2 returns TagSlotDisplay for tags and Composite(per-item displays) for lists. The tree already decodes Composite (protocol SlotDisplay::Composite) and the resolver flattens it in order (recipe_book.rs:757), so both wire forms yield the same ordered item list the local Ingredient.order already keeps.

SignatureValidator#from: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is the authlib package move (com.mojang.authlib.services -> com.mojang.authlib.yggdrasil); both from overloads are byte-identical. The Rust references it in a comment only (secure_chat.rs:47).

Biome#getHeightAdjustedTemperature: 26.3 samples SimplexNoise(discard=true).get(x,z); 26.2 samples PerlinSimplexNoise([0]).getValue(x,z,false). Both are a single simplex octave, seed 1234, no offsets: PerlinSimplexNoise valueFactor is 1.0 for one octave, the 2D sampling math is identical (70.0 * corner sum), and both constructors consume the same random sequence (3x nextDouble, 256x nextInt shuffle; GradientNoise confirms the 26.3 order). The Rust SimplexNoise::with_skipped_offsets(1234) + get2 matches both; only a float-vs-double return (<=1 ulp, unobservable through the 0.15 snow threshold) differs.

FileToIdConverter#listMatchingResources: 26.3 routes through an extensionSelector() helper and added prefixMatches/matches; 26.2 calls manager.listResources(prefix, this::extensionMatches) directly. Same prefix, same predicate, identical behaviour. The Rust references it in a comment only (lan/data.rs:186).

GuiEntityRenderer#renderToTexture: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is PoseStack.rotate(quaternion) vs mulPose(quaternion) — a rename of the same pose multiply. The Rust emit_preview takes pre-transformed quads and ports no rotation.

Display#getInterpolatedBoundingBox exists only in 26.3 (culling box shifted by the interpolated position delta); 26.2 has getBoundingBoxForCulling() returning the raw box at the tick position. PORTED: both display_in_view call sites now pass display.position (tick) instead of the interpolated render position; the geometry still renders interpolated. Doc comment updated.

BiomeManager#getBiome: 26.3 split the BlockPos form into a delegating overload plus getBiome(int,int,int) and renamed BiomeResolver to NoiseBiomeSource; the body (x-2, >>2 zoom) is identical. The Rust ports the lookup in mesher.rs unchanged.

PatchedDataComponentMap#set: 26.3 stores the patch as raw Object with a Removed sentinel, 26.2 as Optional (empty = removed). The set/remove semantics are identical: value==default drops the patch entry, otherwise the value is stored, and the return is the previous value or the default. The Rust's comments (stations.rs:487,608,750) describe semantics true in both versions.
JumpableVehicleBar#extractBackground: the decompiled classes are identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (the changed flag is a bytecode-level artefact); the Rust jump_bar ports it unchanged.

Items#mapProperties exists only in 26.3 (a helper returning MAP_DECORATIONS EMPTY); 26.2 registers FILLED_MAP inline with MAP_DECORATIONS EMPTY plus MAP_COLOR DEFAULT (4603950). The empty-decorations elision in encode_components holds in both versions; the prototype's map_color comes from the 26.2 prepared data. Comment updated to the 26.2 registration.

ClockManager#getInstance exists only in 26.3 (returns a ClockInstance); 26.2's interface has getTotalTicks(Holder<WorldClock>) returning the ticks directly — same observable value, API shape only. All four 26.2 timelines use clock minecraft:overworld, whose total ticks are the day time, so the Rust clock callback (|_clock| at.day_time) is exactly right. Comment updated to the 26.2 API.

Pack#readPackMetadata: bodies identical except 26.3 opens via resources.openMetadata (PackMetadataResources) and 26.2 via resources.openPrimary (PackResources) — a 26.3 API split; the metadata parsing logic is unchanged. The Rust references it in a comment only (datapack.rs:172).

DebugLevelSource#buildTerrain exists only in 26.3 (ChunkGenerator step restructure); 26.2 has fillFromNoise returning the chunk unchanged plus an empty buildSurface — both no-ops, same as 26.3's buildTerrain. The Rust builds the debug chunk directly; comment updated to the 26.2 step names.

TextDisplayRenderer#submitInner: 26.2 inlines the background as custom geometry at TEXT_BACKGROUND_OFFSET (-0.01) and orders text after it; 26.3 uses submitTextBackground plus the same POLYGON_OFFSET/SEE_THROUGH text modes. The Rust draws the background quad at depth -0.01 (text_display.rs draw) and the text on the polygon-offset layer, background first — matching 26.2's observable geometry. Comment updated to the 26.2 form.

ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity#updateState: 26.3 calls level.setBlockAndUpdate, 26.2 calls level.setBlock(pos, state, 3). Bytecode confirms setBlockAndUpdate == setBlock(..., 3) in both versions. The Rust uses flags::UPDATE_ALL (3). Comment updated.

ProtoChunk#setBlockState: 26.3 updates existing heightmaps inline then primes the missing ones; 26.2 collects the missing ones, primes, then updates ALL. Observationally equivalent: after priming from current state (which includes the new block), update() is a no-op — an opaque new block is already below firstAvailable, and a non-opaque one either returns early or rescans to the same height (verified against 26.2 Heightmap.update/primeHeightmaps). The Rust follows the 26.3 order. Bonus: 26.2's Heightmap predicate is BlockStateBase::blocksMotion (not the 26.3 tag), confirming the per-state motion port.

InputQuirks#isQuitShortcutDown exists only in 26.3 (SDL-era InputQuirks); 26.2's class is the older GLFW-era form without it. The Rust function serves the Horizon quit_shortcuts setting (allow platform quit shortcuts to close the window), and the keys (Cmd+Q macOS, Alt+F4 elsewhere) are platform conventions, not version-specific vanilla behaviour. Function kept; comment updated to note the 26.3-only provenance.

Heightmap#primeHeightmaps: 26.3 uses index-based removal from a copied list, 26.2 an iterator with back(size) rewind — the same top-down scan (first non-air state matching each type's predicate sets height y+1, break when all found). The predicate differs (26.3 tag vs 26.2 blocksMotion), already handled by the per-state motion port feeding the Rust predicates. The Rust prime() implements the same scan.

OverlayRecipeComponent#extractRenderState decompiles identically in 26.3 and 26.2. The class's only diff is mouseClicked's button constant (1 in 26.3 SDL, 0 in 26.2 GLFW — both mean left button), a method this item does not name and the Rust does not port (recipe_book_screen.rs draws the overlay; input uses winit buttons).
CrafterScreen#extractBackground: the decompiled classes are identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (the changed flag is a bytecode-level artefact); the Rust crafter() ports it unchanged.

StreamCodec#composite: 26.3 added 13- and 14-arity overloads (Function13/14); the 1-12 arity overloads are identical. The Rust packet! macro mirrors composite for any field count, so the added overloads are irrelevant.

WardenSpawnTracker#tryWarn: 26.2's ServerPlayer.getWardenSpawnTracker returns Optional<WardenSpawnTracker>, 26.3's returns the tracker directly — but 26.2's is always Optional.of(tracker), never empty, so the .map/.flatMap/.ifPresent calls are equivalent to direct calls. The Rust try_warn over a tracker slice matches both.

CreakingHeartBlockEntity#serverTick: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is setBlockAndUpdate -> setBlock(pos, state, 3) in two places, proven identical by bytecode (item 253). The Rust ports serverTick's logic unchanged.

TitleScreen#init: 26.3 adds an isOfflineDeveloperMode() check to the friends button and drops a constructor arg from OptionsScreen; neither changes the buttons' add order or positions, which is all key_focus.rs ports (tab-order test).

PathNavigation#moveTo: 26.3 added a moveTo(Entity, int reachRange, double) overload; 26.2's moveTo(Entity, double) inlines createPath(target, 1). The 2-arg form is identical (reach 1). The Rust calls nav_move_to_entity(w, at, 1, speed).

PrimedTnt#tick: 26.3 added setRequiresPrecisePosition(horizontalCollision || verticalCollision) and getMoveSimulationType() (SERVER_AND_CLIENT); 26.2 has neither. The fuse/fall/bounce/smoke logic is identical, and the Rust client-side TNT tick ports that unchanged. Nuance (out of scope, negligible): 26.2's ServerEntity full-syncs TNT only when onGround changes, while the Rust lan_entities sets precise whenever on the ground (the 26.3 rule); a resting TNT's deltas are 0 either way, so nothing player-visible differs.

LevelLoadingScreen#extractBackground: the method body is identical; the class diff is only the static chunk-status colour map (26.3 TERRAIN 3159410 vs 26.2 NOISE 13750737 / SURFACE 7497737 / CARVERS 3159410), which the Rust does not port anywhere (no colour constant appears in the tree). The Rust ports only the Reason-based background.

Ravager#blockedByItem: the Ravager override is the same in both (50% stun, else fling; syncVelocity is 26.3's rename of hurtMarked; fullyBlocked unused in the body). But the base LivingEntity.blockedByItem differs: 26.3 skips the 0.5 knockback when fully blocked, 26.2 knocks back unconditionally. Ported: shield.rs blocked_by_attacker now knocks back unconditionally and the fully parameter is removed (dealDefaultKnockback's own fully-blocked gate is identical in both versions, so health.rs is untouched).

CaveVines#use: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is the loot call's signature (26.3 passes pos as an extra loot-context argument); the table (HARVEST_CAVE_VINE) and state are the same. The Rust fox port drops 1 glow berry and clears berries, matching both.

Witch#performRangedAttack: 26.3 replaced the hardcoded 8.0F uncertainty with rangedAttackUncertainty(level), which returns 8.0F for witches; the potion selection, speeds (0.45/0.75) and aim (yd + dist*0.2) are identical. The Rust uses 8.0.
SharedConstants#getProtocolVersion: the pin differs (777 in 26.3, 776 in 26.2) and the tree already carries PROTOCOL_VERSION = 776 from the ladder re-base.

ClientInformation#write: 26.3 encodes the three enums via STREAM_CODEC, 26.2 via writeEnum — both write the ordinal as a varint, same field order, same wire bytes. The Rust adapter writes varints and drops particle_status for 1.21.1, matching both.

ServerExplosion#hurtEntities: two diffs. (1) 26.3 gates damage on source.doTeamsAllowDamage(entity); 26.2 has no team check — explosions hurt team mates. Ported: removed the teams_allow closure, the player hurtable gate (explosion_hurt_player's exploding param dropped) and hurt_mob's hurtable param; the teammate test case now documents the 26.2 rule. (2) 26.3 calls pushFromExplosion, 26.2 push — but 26.3's pushFromExplosion is just push(impulse), so the Rust push_from_explosion is unchanged.

WanderingTrader#mobInteract: 26.3 returns SUCCESS_SERVER for trading, 26.2 returns SUCCESS (which swings the hand). SUCCESS_SERVER itself exists in 26.2 (spawn eggs still return it in both versions). Ported in remote_mob_use.rs: mob_swings' trader arm now swings except for spawn eggs (SUCCESS_SERVER) and leads (CONSUME), and the name-tag branch swings in both cases (unnamed falls through to trading, SUCCESS in 26.2). Test assertions added. Follow-up: the horse fedFood and panda bamboo arms in the same function still encode SUCCESS_SERVER and are unverified for 26.2 (no rank-2 item names them).

UnderwaterAmbientSoundHandler#tick: only a class rename (26.3 UnderLiquidSubSound vs 26.2 UnderwaterAmbientSoundInstances.SubSound); thresholds (1e-4/0.001/0.01), sounds and tickDelay logic are identical. The Rust tick_underwater matches both.

ItemUtils#createFilledResult: the only diff is 26.3's player.drop(stack, false, Prediction.PREDICTED) vs 26.2's player.drop(stack, false) — the Prediction argument belongs to 26.3's prediction system, which 26.2 lacks; the drop itself is identical. The Rust filled() has no Prediction concept and ports the drop unchanged.
CrafterBlockEntity#serverTick: the only diff is setBlockAndUpdate -> setBlock(pos, state, 3), proven identical by bytecode (item 253).

BeaconMenu#removed: the only diff is 26.3's player.drop(stack, false, Prediction.SERVER_ONLY) vs 26.2's player.drop(stack, false) — the Prediction argument belongs to 26.3's prediction system; the drop is identical. The Rust drops the payment with no Prediction concept.
LoomScreen#extractBackground: the decompiled classes are identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (the changed flag is a bytecode-level artefact).

ResultSlot#onTake: the only diff is 26.3's player.drop(replacement, false, Prediction.PREDICTED) vs 26.2's player.drop(replacement, false) — the Prediction argument belongs to 26.3's prediction system; the remainder drop is identical. The Rust ports the remainder handling with no Prediction concept.
ModelPart#translateAndRotate: only poseStack.rotate -> mulPose (same rename as item 217); the ZYX rotation and /16 translation are identical. The Rust applies glam EulerRot::ZYX, matching both.

PiglinAi#throwItemsTowardPos: 26.3 calls swing(OFF_HAND, SwingAnimation.DEFAULT), 26.2 calls swing(OFF_HAND) — the default animation either way (the piglin's off hand carries no swing_animation component). The Rust swings the off hand with SwingAnimation::DEFAULT.
AbstractVillager#addOffersFromTradeSet: only tradeSet.trades() -> tradeSet.getTrades() (26.3 made TradeSet a record; 26.2's class has a getter). Same offers, same duplicates handling.

Fireworks#addToTooltip: 26.3 uses translatable flight_duration with a %s argument; 26.2 builds translatable flight + SPACE + number. 26.2's lang has NO flight_duration key (only flight = 'Flight Duration:'), so the Rust's 26.3 form rendered the raw key. Ported: the flight line now uses the flight key + space + number; the test's fake lang now carries the 26.2 key. Expected lines unchanged ('Flight Duration: 1').
Phantom#tick: only the playLocalSound call form (26.3's entity overload vs 26.2's positional overload with a trailing false); same sound, same volume/pitch draws (0.95 + rand*0.05 twice).

Dolphin#registerGoals: 26.3 uses TryFindLiquidGoal with the DOLPHIN_TRIES_TO_FIND tag, 26.2 uses TryFindWaterGoal. The Rust already ports the 26.2 form (TryFindWater seeking Fluid::Water, goals.rs:2714).

LongJump#canRun: the only diff is the fluid gate — 26.3 inlines isInFluidDeeperThan(threshold, ENTITY_FLOATABLE) || isInLava(), 26.2 calls Swim.shouldSwim (isInWater && water height > threshold || isInLava). ENTITY_FLOATABLE is water only, so the gates are equivalent. The Rust uses Mob::floats() (water > threshold || in lava), matching both.

TrialSpawner$FullConfig#overrideEntityData: 26.3-only (with TrialSpawnerBlockEntity.setEntityData and BaseSpawner.setEntityData). 26.2's SpawnEggItem.useOn always calls setEntityId(type) — an op's egg data is never applied, on trial or regular spawners. Ported: spawn_egg_on_spawner returns only the id, use_spawn_egg_on_spawner drops its data parameter, override_entity_data and Spawner.set_entity_data removed (with the 26.3-only merge test, which pinned behaviour 26.2 lacks).

Font#prepareBackground: 26.3-only helper (creates the background effect at z=-0.01); 26.2's TextDisplayRenderer inlines the same -0.01 background geometry (item 252). The Rust already draws the background 0.01 behind; only the comment's citation updated to the 26.2 form.

AttributeTrackSampler#applyTimeBased: only the clock API (26.3 clockManager.getInstance(clock).totalTicks() vs 26.2 clockManager.getTotalTicks(clock)) — the same API-shape difference as item 237, same value. The Rust apply() takes the tick count as a parameter; the caller passes day time.

NbtUtils readBlockState/writeBlockState: the diff is exactly the Name/Properties vs id/properties codec form. The read side already accepts both forms. Write side fixed: save_nbt palette now writes Name/Properties (was id/properties), test assertion updated; also fixed BlockState::to_nbt (chunk.rs:192) to write Name/Properties — chunk palettes in 'id' form would be unreadable by vanilla 26.2. No test pins the 'id' write form for chunks; read sides accept both, so round-trips stay safe.

WorldBorderRenderer: 26.3's rebuildWorldBorderBuffer applies RENDERING_OFFSET (0.01) to the border bounds; 26.2 uses the bounds as-is (no such constant in 26.2). Removed the OFFSET const and its application from rebuild(). The rest matches 26.2: v0/v1 texture coords, rebuild condition (needs_rebuild || border != last_border), closest-border sides, transform math. The 26.3 OIT render-pass plumbing is moot — the Rust module is GPU-free by design.

PauseScreen: extractRenderState identical (music.rs's use: no-change). createPauseMenu differs in the bottom buttons (port landed in screens.rs pause_buttons): 26.3 shows OPTIONS + WORLD_OPTIONS when level != null; 26.2 shows OPTIONS + MULTIPLAYER_OPTIONS when hasSingleplayerServer(), else a single full-width OPTIONS. Ported: single-player -> OPTIONS (98, id 1) + MULTIPLAYER_OPTIONS (98, id 9); multiplayer -> full-width OPTIONS (204, id 1). Documented gap: id 9 still opens the existing 26.3 WorldOptionsScreen (which holds the LAN publish controls, the functional core of 26.2's MultiplayerOptionsScreen); a dedicated 26.2 MultiplayerOptionsScreen layout port is outstanding. The friend-list listener and friends-button condition differences have no Rust equivalent.

PlacedFeature: getFeatures is a pure type rename (ConfiguredFeature -> Feature in 26.3, same logic). place: 26.3 routes through the 26.3-only FeaturePlacer class (explicit stack, reverse-push to preserve order); 26.2 uses placeWithContext (stream flatMap). Both traversals are depth-first, in-order, with identical random-draw order, and the Rust FeaturePlacer (chain.rs) implements the stack form with the same order guarantees. The 4-arg place's biomeCheck flag maps exactly onto 26.2's place() (Optional.empty()) vs placeWithBiomeCheck() (Optional.of(this)).

Camera: getFluidInCamera identical. extractRenderState differs only in arg shape (26.3 takes DeltaTracker and stores partial ticks in the state; 26.2 takes the float directly) plus 26.3 setting isFirstPerson on the render state, which 26.2 never sets. The Rust fov.rs derives first_person from camera_type directly and never reads an isFirstPerson field, so the difference does not affect it.

FallingBlockEntity fall/tick: setBlockAndUpdate vs setBlock(..., 3) is literally identical in 26.2 (setBlockAndUpdate IS setBlock(pos, state, 3)). The tick differences are 26.3-only additions the Rust does not implement: the ClientboundAddTransientBlockPacket send on landing and setRequiresPrecisePosition. The fixture compares landing decisions, changed cells and level events only — no packet or precise-position surface. The landing decision logic itself is unchanged.
SnowGolem: 26.3 extracts the ranged-attack uncertainty into rangedAttackUncertainty() returning 12.0F; 26.2 hardcodes 12.0F at the shoot call. Same value. The Rust golem.rs already shoots with 12.0.

Item: getPlayerPOVHitResult differs only in the view-vector call's spelling — 26.3 Player.calculateViewVector (static) vs 26.2 player.calculateViewVector (final instance); the Entity.calculateViewVector body is identical in both versions and the Rust view_vector matches it. useOn: 26.3 checks the BLOCK_TRANSFORMER data component; 26.2 returns PASS. The Rust generic use-on path has no component check (26.2's per-item transforms are the rank-1 block transformer), matching 26.2.

Pufferfish playerTouch/touch: 26.3 gates the sting behind doTeamsAllowDamage; 26.2 has no team check — teammates sting too. Ported: removed the teams_allow_damage check from both the player-touch path (pufferfish_player.rs) and the mob-touch path (aquatic.rs sting_touching_mobs), with the now-unused import and team lookup removed.

Shulker: teleportSomewhere identical. createInterpolationHandler is 26.3-only and returns NO_OP; 26.2 has no such method. The Rust already treats a move packet as a snap to setPos with no interpolation, which is the same observable behaviour. Comments updated to cite the 26.2 form.

WinScreen: extractBackground identical. keyPressed/keyReleased differ only in key encoding — 26.2 event.key() 341/345 (GLFW left/right control) vs 26.3 event.shortcutKey() 1073742048/1073742052 (SDL left/right control): the same physical keys. The Rust win_screen.rs Key enum admits only Up/Space/LeftControl/RightControl (from_code returns None otherwise), so only control keys ever reach speedup_modifiers, matching both versions.

AccountProfileKeyPairManager.fetchProfileKeyPair differs only in the authlib import (com.mojang.authlib.services.response in 26.3 vs yggdrasil.response in 26.2) — same class, moved package; the method body is identical. ClientHandshakePacketListenerImpl.authenticateServer differs only in a log line ('Authentication failed: {}' vs the bare message). CopperGolem: turnToStatue identical. mobInteract: 26.3 adds an explicit HONEYCOMB_WAX_ON playSound on waxing; 26.2 fires only level event 3003. The Rust already implements the 26.2 form (level_event_at(3003) with the comment 'The event carries the wax-on sound in 26.2; no explicit play').

Sniffer.isTempted: 26.2 reads the IS_TEMPTED boolean memory, which FollowTemptation sets on start and erases on stop (verified by scanning the jars: only FollowTemptation, MemoryModuleType and Sniffer reference it in 26.2); 26.3 reads TEMPTING_PLAYER presence, true whenever a tempting player is sensed — including during the 100-tick temptation cooldown. Ported: added an is_tempted memory slot (animal_brain.rs), set in FollowTemptation try_start (with the VALUE_ABSENT start guard) and cleared in do_stop; is_tempted now reads it. emitDiggingParticles: no change needed — the Rust already plays the hit sound positionally at the sniffer (26.2's coords form with distanceDelay=false), and a digging sniffer does not move, so 26.3's entity-bound form is equivalent.
